title: New Music Discovery Ratio
dataSources: Tautulli/Plex playback (`tautulli:play`), Jellyfin activity (`jellyfin:activity`), Spotify recently-played (`spotify:play`), Steam player and achievements (`steam:player`), Sonarr events (`sonarr:event`).
app: Plex / Jellyfin (Tautulli), Sonos, Spotify, Steam, Xbox/PSN, and the *arr stack (Sonarr/Radarr) APIs and webhooks via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count as plays, sum(eval(first_time_artist="true")) as new_artist_plays by _time
| eval discovery_pct=round(100*new_artist_plays/plays,1)
| where plays>0
| sort - _time
description: Measures how much of your week was spent on genuinely new artists instead of familiar favourites, a simple metric for whether you are exploring or looping.
value: Discovery is one of the joys of streaming, but recommendation feeds often collapse into comfort-zone repetition; this ratio keeps that honest.
implementation: Forward a first-time-artist marker from your playback export or enrichment job; review weekly discovery percentage over time.
visualization: Weekly line chart of new-artist play percentage.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Spotify — Spotify Web API recently-played → HEC.
• **Subcategory context**: Media, Gaming & Entertainment — typical feeds: Tautulli/Plex playback (`tautulli:play`), Jellyfin activity (`jellyfin:activity`), Spotify recently-played (`spotify:play`), Steam player/achievements (`steam:player`), Sonarr/Radarr events (`sonarr:e.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `spotify:play`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Spotify** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=spotify:play`.

**Collection method:** Spotify Web API recently-played → HEC.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `GET /v1/me/player/recently-played`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 900s.

**Key fields to extract:** `track.name, artist, played_at, duration_ms`.

**Typical connector stack:** Plex / Jellyfin (Tautulli), Sonos, Spotify, Steam, Xbox/PSN, and *arr stack (Sonarr/Radarr) APIs and webhooks via HEC..

**Author notes:** Forward a first-time-artist marker from your playback export or enrichment job; review weekly discovery percentage over time.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "spotify:play", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **New Music Discovery Ratio** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=spotify:play`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `plays` (> 0) after sum — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `plays`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count as plays, sum(eval(first_time_artist="true")) as new_artist_plays by _time
| eval discovery_pct=round(100*new_artist_plays/plays,1)
| where plays>0
| sort - _time
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Spotify app → Recently played. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, plays
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `plays` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(plays) AS p50 perc90(plays) AS p90 perc99(plays) AS p99 max(plays) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.7.16: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Weekly Line Chart Of New-Artist Play Percentage (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Spotify — no Spotify events / missing fields:** If `spotify:play` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Spotify connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Spotify — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Spotify JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=spotify:play | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Spotify — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Spotify — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Spotify APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1w` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1w` buckets.
